brief.situation: You are the security engineer on call at Fernhill Analytics, a fictional company on Azure. At 02:05 an alert says the backup admin account r.khan, signed in from an address it has never used, deleted the backup data of four production VMs on the backup vault bv-prod. Deleting backups first is a common step before ransomware. The deleted backups are soft-deleted for 14 days, but on this vault soft delete can still be turned off. Contain the account, protect what can still be recovered, keep the evidence and report.
handover: You own a Resource Guard in the separate security subscription; nobody in the backup team has rights on it. MUA is not yet turned on for bv-prod.
You have the Security Administrator role in Entra ID and Backup Contributor on bv-prod.
howItWorks: Each task takes analyst time: choose it, then let the work finish, which moves the clock by the minutes that task takes. The attacker keeps working on the same clock.
New alerts and log lines appear in the console as they happen.
When you declare the incident contained, you notify, write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the incident report: what the attacker was doing and why, what you did first and why in that order, and how bv-prod is protected against the next compromised admin.

parts.label: What was happening
parts.criteria: Recognizes deleting backups (and cutting retention, disabling soft delete) as staging for ransomware by a taken-over admin account, from the sign-in and the vault's critical operations.
parts.modelAnswer: r.khan was signed in from a new country after an approved MFA push, cut retention and deleted the backups of four VMs: destroying recovery before ransomware.

parts.label: Order of actions
parts.criteria: Contains the account first (block sign-in, revoke sessions), protects soft delete with MUA, and only then undeletes and resumes protection, because undeleting while the attacker is in is undone; keeps evidence; avoids taking production down when containing the identity is enough.
parts.modelAnswer: I blocked r.khan and revoked its sessions, turned on MUA with the Resource Guard in the security subscription so soft delete could not be disabled, then undeleted the four items and resumed protection, restored retention and exported the logs.

parts.label: Hardening
parts.criteria: MUA with a Resource Guard the backup team cannot control (separate subscription or tenant), soft delete kept on with longer retention, phishing-resistant MFA and least privilege for backup admins.
parts.modelAnswer: bv-prod keeps MUA with a Resource Guard in another subscription that backup admins have no rights on, soft delete stays on with longer retention, and backup admins move to phishing-resistant MFA and just-in-time roles.

expertPath.text: Sign-ins: r.khan from a new country after an approved push. This is a takeover.
Block r.khan's sign-in and revoke its sessions.

contained.headline: Good: contained, backups safe
contained.body: Deleting backups is ransomware's first move. You cut off the identity, put the vault's security settings behind a Resource Guard, then recovered the soft-deleted backups.

containedLate.headline: Contained, with gaps
containedLate.body: The attacker is out. The criteria show what slipped: time, soft delete turned off, a recovery the attacker undid, production shut down, or a step missed.

purged.headline: Backups gone
purged.body: Soft delete only protects while it is on. Block the account first and put MUA in front of the vault's security settings.

encrypted.headline: Ransomware ran

scoring.modelReasoning: A backup admin signed in from a new country after an approved MFA push, cut retention and deleted four VMs' backups: ransomware staging. Block the account and revoke its sessions first; turn on MUA with the Resource Guard in the separate subscription so disabling soft delete, removing MUA or cutting retention needs authorization the backup team cannot give; then undelete and resume protection (doing it while the attacker is in is undone), restore retention, export the logs and escalate. Shutting down production is not needed once the identity is contained.
